key_insight: A human-in-the-loop workflow using SAM can improve pulmonary nodule segmentation by combining iterative human prompting with AI masks.
clinical_relevance: This approach may reduce annotation burden and support faster, scalable, and safer segmentation workflows in chest CT imaging.
method: Built Hi-Seg, a collaborative segmentation framework on top of SAM.
Humans refine prompts through trial-and-error learning and semantic reasoning.
Tested the system across multiple annotator groups on external chest CT datasets.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on chest CT scans from 1,179 patients across 12 centers, where Hi-Seg achieved a mean Dice score of nearly 85% and outperformed 5 deep learning models and 13 SAM variants.
watch_item: Performance depends on iterative human prompting, so real-world deployment will need training, quality control, and workflow integration to avoid inconsistent results.
paper_title: Human and AI collaboration for pulmonary nodule segmentation
